title: Neural organoid models of human brain evolution
title_zh: 人脑进化的神经类器官模型
abstract: The human brain has structural and functional differences to our closest living relatives, the other great apes. It is thought that these differences give rise to many of the traits we associate with being human, such as our prodigious capacity to learn and be creative. However, the molecular mechanisms that underpin these differences are mostly unknown. In this review, we describe how neural organoids, an in vitro model of brain development, enable questions of human brain evolution to be functionally investigated in evolutionarily relevant developmental contexts. We discuss new insights at the genetic, cellular, and developmental scales and highlight current challenges in organoid generation, in long-term culture, and in establishing multimodal phenotypic measurements. We anticipate expanding the application of organoid models across Mammalia to help us better define species- and lineage-specific traits and improve our understanding of how complex traits emerge and evolve across developmental and evolutionary timescales.
abstract_zh: 人脑与我们最近的现存亲属——其他大猿——在结构和功能上存在差异。人们认为，这些差异孕育了我们与人类相关的许多特征，例如我们非凡的学习和创造能力。然而，支撑这些差异的分子机制大多未知。在本综述中，我们描述了神经类器官（一种脑发育的体外模型）如何使人类脑进化的问题能够在进化相关的发育背景下得到功能性研究。我们讨论了在遗传、细胞和发育尺度上的新见解，并强调了类器官生成、长期培养以及建立多模态表型测量方面的当前挑战。我们预期，将类器官模型的应用扩展到哺乳动物类中，将有助于我们更好地界定物种特有和谱系特有的特征，并提高我们对复杂特征如何在发育和进化时间尺度上出现和演化的理解。
